questions.question: Which of the following plants can be made to climb walls using special support?
questions.solution:
The Pumpkin plant is a creeper that can be made to climb walls or trellises using its tendrils for support.
  • Tendrils are specialized thread-like structures that sensitive to touch and coil around objects they contact.
  • Note: Rose and Lemon plants are shrubs with woody stems, and Sunflowers are erect herbs that do not naturally climb.

questions.question: Which species of green algae, commonly known as stonewort, is often mistaken for a plant?
questions.solution:
Chara is a genus of green algae that is commonly known as stonewort.
  • It is often mistaken for a land plant because of its stem-like and leaf-like structures and its upright growth.
  • The name 'stonewort' comes from the fact that these algae can become encrusted with calcium carbonate deposits, making them feel rough and stony.

questions.question: Which of the following plants is a Pteridophyte which is usually found in moist, shady places or gardens and on hills where the temperatures are low?
questions.solution:
Ferns are a well-known group of Pteridophytes that thrive in moist, shady, and cool environments.
  • Pteridophytes are vascular plants that reproduce via spores rather than seeds.
  • Note: Riccia and Sphagnum are Bryophytes (mosses/liverworts), and Porphyra is a type of red algae.

questions.question: What is the chemical name of the substance that forms the tooth enamel in the human body?
questions.solution:
The chemical name of the substance that forms tooth enamel is Calcium hydroxyapatite.
  • Tooth enamel is the hardest substance in the human body.
  • It is a crystalline mineral form of calcium phosphate ($Ca_{10}(PO_4)_6(OH)_2$).

questions.question: Animals where the fertilisation of eggs and the development of the baby up to the fetal stage takes place inside the mother's body are known as _____.
questions.solution:
Animals that give birth to live young ones, where the embryo develops inside the mother's body, are called viviparous.
  • In these animals, the mother provides nutrients to the developing fetus through a placenta.
  • Note: Oviparous animals are those that lay eggs (like birds or reptiles).

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement of the following.
questions.option_1: Vitamin C plays an important role in collagen synthesis.
questions.option_2: Vitamin A, E and C act as antioxidants.
questions.option_3: Fat is considered as a good source of energy during the exercise and competition.
questions.option_4: Vitamin C facilitates absorption and utilisation of iron in the body.
questions.solution:
The statement that 'Fat is considered as a good source of energy during exercise and competition' is technically incorrect in the context of high-intensity performance.
  • While fats provide the highest energy per gram, Carbohydrates are the preferred and most efficient fuel source for high-intensity exercise because they can be broken down faster than fats.
  • Vitamin C is indeed essential for collagen synthesis and iron absorption.

questions.question:
Below are few statements about vaccination. Select the correct statement/s.

Statement A:In vaccination, a preparation of antigenic proteins of pathogens or inactivated/weakened pathogens (vaccine) are introduced into the body.

Statement B:The vaccines generate memory-B and T-cells that recognise the pathogens quickly.
questions.option_1: Both statements A and B Incorrect
questions.option_3: Both statements A and B are correct
questions.solution:
Both statements A and B are correct regarding vaccination.
  • Statement A: Vaccines use antigens or weakened pathogens to stimulate the immune system without causing the disease.
  • Statement B: This process creates memory B and T-cells, which stay in the body to launch a rapid attack if the actual pathogen enters in the future.

questions.question: The saliva helps in the digestion of food in animals. What does it do?
questions.option_1: Helps is sensing taste of food
questions.option_3: Prevents food from entering the wind pipe
questions.solution:
Saliva contains an enzyme called salivary amylase (ptyalin) that breaks down starch into sugar (maltose).
  • This marks the beginning of chemical digestion in the mouth.
  • Saliva also moistens food to help in swallowing.

questions.question: The combination of high levels of which type of fats with low HDL cholesterol or high LDL cholesterol levels can increase the risk of heart attack and stroke?
questions.solution:
High levels of Triglycerides combined with low HDL (good cholesterol) or high LDL (bad cholesterol) significantly increase the risk of atherosclerosis, heart attack, and stroke.
  • Triglycerides are the most common type of fat in the body, storing excess calories from your diet.

questions.question: How does flexibility of the cell membrane help living organisms?
questions.solution:
The flexibility of the cell membrane (specifically in organisms like Amoeba) allows the cell to absorb food and other materials from its external environment.
  • This process of engulfing food by the cell membrane is known as Endocytosis.

questions.question: Xerophthalmia refers to the signs and symptoms of which sense organ related to vitamin A deficiency?
questions.solution:
Xerophthalmia is a progressive eye disease caused by Vitamin A deficiency that affects the Eyes.
  • It begins with night blindness and can progress to severe dryness (conjunctival xerosis) and eventually permanent blindness due to corneal damage.

questions.question: Name the virus spread by mosquitoes that causes inflammation in the brain?
questions.solution:
Japanese encephalitis is a viral infection spread by mosquitoes (specifically the Culex genus) that causes inflammation of the brain (encephalitis).
  • It is most common in rural and agricultural areas of Asia.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement from the following about mitosis.
questions.option_1: The daughter cells have half the number of chromosomes as mother cell.
questions.option_2: Each cell called mother cell divides to form two identical daughter cells.
questions.option_3: It helps in growth and repair of tissues in organisms.
questions.solution:
The statement that 'The daughter cells have half the number of chromosomes as mother cell' is incorrect for mitosis.
  • In Mitosis, daughter cells are genetically identical to the mother cell and have the same number of chromosomes (diploid).
  • The reduction of chromosomes by half occurs in Meiosis.

questions.question: In the context of ecology, what is symbiosis?
questions.option_3: Random movement of organisms in their habitat
questions.option_4: A close and long-term interaction between different species
questions.solution:
Symbiosis refers to a close and long-term interaction between two different biological species.
  • These interactions can be Mutualistic (both benefit), Commensal (one benefits, other is unaffected), or Parasitic (one benefits, other is harmed).

questions.question: Which of the following is the least likely to cause obesity in humans?
questions.solution:
Over consumption of green vegetables is the least likely to cause obesity.
  • Green vegetables are low in calories and high in fibre, which helps in weight management.
  • Genetics, high-fat diets, and sedentary lifestyles are all major contributors to obesity.

questions.question: In a forest ecosystem of Grass → Impala → Hyena, if all the Hyenas are taken away, what will happen ultimately?
questions.option_2: Grass land will not be affected.
questions.option_4: Impala will die of starvation due to higher population.
questions.solution:
In a food chain (Grass $ ightarrow$ Impala $ ightarrow$ Hyena), if the top predator (Hyena) is removed, the Impala population will die of starvation due to overpopulation.
  • Without predators, the Impala population grows unchecked until they consume all available grass, leading to an ecosystem collapse and mass starvation.

questions.question: The fluid portion of the cytosol, devoid of any cell organelles, present in both the prokaryotic and eukaryotic cell is ____________.
questions.solution:
Hyaloplasm (also known as the ground substance of the cytosol) is the fluid portion of the cytoplasm that remains when all organelles are removed.
  • It is found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells and serves as the site for many metabolic reactions like glycolysis.

questions.question: Which member of the phylum Porifera is the oldest metazoan group still existing on our planet?
questions.solution:
Sponges (Phylum Porifera) are considered the oldest metazoan (multicellular animal) group still in existence.
  • They have existed for over 600 million years and possess a very simple body plan without true tissues or organs.

questions.question: If a fish eats a shrimp, the energy gets transferred from:
questions.solution:
In this scenario, energy is transferred from a primary consumer (shrimp) to a secondary consumer (fish).
  • The shrimp eats producers (algae), making it a primary consumer. The fish that eats the shrimp becomes the secondary consumer.

questions.question: The physiological state which decreases appetite and indicates the feeling of fullness is known as _______________.
questions.solution:
Satiety is the physiological state of feeling full and satisfied after eating, which inhibits the urge to consume more food.
  • It is regulated by hormones like Leptin and Cholecystokinin (CCK).

questions.question: Organisms, when faced with new circumstances and surroundings, start adapting new characters to fit into their environment. This is termed as _____________.
questions.solution:
Behavioural adaptation occurs when an organism changes its actions or habits to survive in a new environment.
  • Examples include migration, hibernation, or changing foraging patterns.

questions.question: Large deposits of iron in the liver leads to a condition called _________________.
questions.solution:
Hemosiderosis is a condition characterized by the excessive focal deposition of iron (in the form of hemosiderin) in organs like the liver.
  • Note: Kwashiorkor is protein deficiency, and Osteomalacia is Vitamin D deficiency.

questions.question: Basal bodies and centrioles show nearly the same fine structure. Which of the following statements sets them apart from each other?
questions.option_1: Basal bodies are protein structures whereas centriole is not at all proteinaceous.
questions.option_2: Centriole has membrane but basal bodies are non-membranous.
questions.option_3: Centriole take part in protein synthesis whereas basal bodies are not involved in this.
questions.option_4: Centrioles possess distal appendages but basal bodies do not carry such things.
questions.solution:
A key structural difference is that Centrioles possess distal appendages while basal bodies do not (though basal bodies are essentially centrioles that have migrated to the cell surface).
  • Distal appendages on the centriole are crucial for its role in docking to the cell membrane to form a cilium or flagellum.

questions.question:
Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?

Nucleus - Storage of genetic information

Ribosome - Protein synthesis

Lysosome - Suicidal bags

Mitochondria - Lipid metabolism
questions.solution:
The pair 'Mitochondria - Lipid metabolism' is not correctly matched as its primary role.
  • The primary function of Mitochondria is ATP production (cellular respiration), earning it the name 'Powerhouse of the cell.'
  • Lipid metabolism primarily occurs in the Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER).

questions.question: The animal cells are arranged in two embryonic layer and one undifferentiated layer that is called _____________.
questions.solution:
In diploblastic animals (like jellyfish), the mesoglea is the undifferentiated, jelly-like layer present between the outer ectoderm and the inner endoderm.
  • Unlike the mesoderm in triploblastic animals, the mesoglea does not contain true cellular tissue.

questions.question:
Select the correct option about typhoid fever in human beings.

Statement A: Streptococcus pneumonia is a pathogenic bacterium which causes typhoid.

Statement B: Typhoid fever could be confirmed by widal test.

Statement C: Typhoid causes Intestinal perforation.
questions.option_1: All statements A, B and C correct
questions.option_2: Statements B and C are correct
questions.option_3: Statements A and B are correct
questions.solution:
Statements B and C are correct regarding typhoid fever.
  • Statement A is incorrect because Typhoid is caused by Salmonella typhi, not Streptococcus pneumoniae (which causes pneumonia).
  • Typhoid is confirmed by the Widal test and can lead to severe complications like intestinal perforation if left untreated.
